stage: 1 of 2: discovery, licence review and manifest. Nothing has been built and nothing has been moved into the repository.
repositoryPolicy: no third-party ROM binary and no third-party source has been committed to GU; this manifest is the only artefact proposed for the repository, and it contains metadata written by me, not third-party code
independence: none of these candidates is derived from the three in-house generators (make_agod_test_rom.py, make_agod_sacrifice_rom.py, make_agod_rate_trap_rom.py): different authors, real games, no shared code or layout rules
freezeRule: the selected list is frozen before any benchmarking run; this manifest is a proposal and is not frozen yet
oracleDiscipline: these cartridges have no oracle. No closed label exists for them, so objective discovery on them is unlabelled by construction and scoring will require a separately recorded judgement, made after discovery, never before

toolchain.sourceAvailable: https://github.com/cc65/cc65 is reachable and buildable from source with gcc and make
toolchain.status: NOT BUILT: the permission classifier denied running make on externally downloaded code (reason: Code from External). Stage 2 needs either that permission or another route.

blockers: building any candidate is blocked: cc65 is absent, apt has no cc65 package, and executing an external build (including building cc65 itself from source) was denied by the permission classifier
no candidate ships a prebuilt .nes in its tree, so there is no build-free path to a ROM from this set
www.nesdev.org is denied by the environment network policy, so the usual homebrew directories could not be browsed; discovery went through web search and GitHub only

candidates.licenseVerified: read from the cloned tree at the pinned revision
candidates.redistribution: permitted under GPL-3.0; distributing a built ROM obliges offering the corresponding source
restrictions: if a built ROM is ever redistributed, the corresponding source must be offered
candidates.reason: a substantial metroidvania: the most behaviourally interesting candidate, with resources, mode changes and progression, which is what the POSITIVE rule needs testing against

candidates.name: NovaTheSquirrel
candidates.licenseVerified: code licence read from LICENSE.txt; asset terms read from README.md at the pinned revision
candidates.redistribution: restricted: a built ROM contains CC-BY-NC-SA assets, so it may not be sold, and the author states the Nova character and design may not be used elsewhere
candidates.researchUse: permitted for non-commercial research as far as the stated terms go
restrictions: character and design use not granted
most dialogue characters are cameos of real people the author asks not be reused
candidates.reason: usable as a local research input, but NOT proposed for the repository: the NonCommercial asset terms and the explicit character restriction make committing a built ROM the wrong default to take on the user's behalf

candidates.name: nesgame
candidates.licenseVerified: no licence, copying or copyright file at the pinned revision
candidates.reason: no licence file: condition 4 rejects anything whose redistribution or research use cannot be established. Absence of a licence is not permission.

candidates.reason: no licence file; same rule as nesgame. Also a work in progress, which makes its behaviour a poor evaluation target.
